# scripts/

## generate-image.mjs

This script generates images for Dixi through the OpenAI Images API. It needs Node 20 or newer and has no dependencies: it uses the built-in `fetch`, `FormData` and `Blob`.

- **Without `--ref`** it calls `POST /v1/images/generations`, which makes an image from text.
- **With one or more `--ref`** it calls `POST /v1/images/edits` as multipart, with one `image[]` field per reference. Use this to composite or restyle existing images, for example to combine component shots into a hero image.
- It decodes `b64_json`, writes the PNG, creates folders as needed and prints the path, the dimensions and the model it used.
- It writes a **sidecar** `<image>.png.json` next to every image. The sidecar records the prompt, model, endpoint, references, size, quality, token usage and creation time, with `"ai_generated": true` and `"label": "AI concept"`. This keeps every AI visual traceable and lets the UI label it.

### Usage

```bash
# single image
node scripts/generate-image.mjs \
  --prompt "Isometric illustration of three translucent layers, no text" \
  --out web/public/images/layers.png --size 1536x1024 --quality medium

# edit / composite from references
node scripts/generate-image.mjs --prompt "Combine these into one clean hero shot" \
  --ref web/public/images/a.png --ref web/public/images/b.png \
  --out web/public/images/hero.png --size 1536x1024

# batch from a prompt file (array of {name, prompt, size, quality, background, ref?})
node scripts/generate-image.mjs --prompt-file scripts/prompts/landing.json
node scripts/generate-image.mjs --prompt-file scripts/prompts/landing.json --only product-dashboard
```

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--size` | `1536x1024`, `1024x1024`, `1024x1536`, `auto` | API default |
| `--quality` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `auto` | API default |
| `--background` | `transparent`, `opaque`, `auto` | API default |
| `--model` | any image model id | see below |
| `--n` | 1–10 | 1 (extra images are saved as `name-2.png`, …) |
| `--out-dir` | output folder for `--prompt-file` | `web/public/images` |
| `--only` | comma-separated names from the prompt file | all |

**Model selection**
- `--model` uses exactly the model you name.
- Otherwise the script tries `OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL` (if set), then `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, then `gpt-image-2`, then `gpt-image-1`. It moves to the next model only when the API rejects the model id.
- `gpt-image-2.5-flare` was verified as working on 2026-10-10.

### API key

- The key is read from `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY`. If it is not set there, the script parses the repo-root `.env`, which is git-ignored through `.env` / `.env.*` in `.gitignore`. Quotes, `export` and comments are handled.
- The script never prints, logs or writes the key. Error messages show only the HTTP status and the API's error message.
- Never commit `.env`, and never paste the key into prompts, sidecars or docs.

### Cost

- Each call is billed by image output tokens, so cost grows with size and quality.
- Measured on 2026-10-10 with `gpt-image-2.5-flare`:
  - 1536x1024 at high quality: about 1,400 output tokens.
  - 1536x1024 at medium quality: about 350 output tokens.
- Check the current per-token price on OpenAI's pricing page. Use `low` or `medium` quality while you iterate, and switch to `high` only for the final hero image.
- The `usage` block in each sidecar is the record of what a given image cost.

content.text:
The Analytics page now shows one social post per profile, with an AI-generated image and a short story built from what customers in that market asked for. I tested it on a 7 Series USA generation and there were no errors.

**What each post card shows:**
- **Header:** the profile as the account, e.g. "Tech-forward · Concept test · 7 Series · USA", with a "Best" badge on the leader.
- **Image:** a square scene with a headline over it and a visible **"AI-generated image"** label (EU AI Act).
- **After the test:** likes, comments, shares and the share of positive reactions. Before the test, the posts appear as "Ready to post".
- **Story and hashtags:** for example #Next7Series #Techforward #USA #ConceptTest.

**How the story is written:** it names the problem customers told us about, then the feeling once it's solved, and closes with a wishlist item when the profile has one. Example for Fix the basics:
> "Drivers in the USA told us what gets in the way every morning: better phone connectivity (CarPlay, Bluetooth), stronger climate control with easy controls and faster, more stable infotainment. The next 7 Series fixes the basics first. No workarounds, no second tries: you get in, and it just works."

Each profile has its own mood:

| Profile | Headline | Scene |
|---|---|---|
| Fix the basics | "Every drive starts calm." | Calm city sunrise, phone connecting on the charging pad, simple physical buttons |
| Tech-forward | "The road ahead, upgraded." | Night highway, glowing digital cockpit and driver assistance |
| Comfort & craft | "Arrive as rested as you left." | Golden hour, stitched leather, wood trim, panoramic roof |

**The images:**
- **What I made:** 9 images with your OpenAI key (3 series × 3 stories), in `web/public/images/posts/`. They cost about 440 output tokens each at medium quality.
- **Rules:** no logos, badges, text, plates or faces; people appear only from behind. Each image has a file next to it recording the prompt, and the prompts are in `scripts/prompts/posts.json` so they can be regenerated.
- **Comfort & craft:** the image model made these as four-panel collages, which reads like a carousel post. I kept them; I can regenerate them as single shots if you prefer.
- **Fixed per car:** the image depends only on the series and the profile type, while the story text changes with the market and that generation's requests.

**Still simulated:** no real posts are made and the reactions are not real; the page says so. With a real social channel connected, these numbers would come from actual posts.
also in the weisghts settings, i want a input that as a manager i can sen d a natural text and the ai will send the right weidhts to setup this, laso make sure is in architecture and UI.

- **On the Settings page:** a "Describe it in your words" box. You write something like *"For the 7 Series, past rejects should count for longer, and don't let social trends push things much"*.
- **The AI:** proposes the matching weights with a short explanation and a before/after comparison. You **apply** or discard.
- **Change log:** each applied change is logged with who, when and the instruction.
- **Without an AI key** (e.g. on Vercel), a simple keyword-based fallback still works.

## Route Handlers
Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.

> **Good to know**: Route Handlers are only available inside the `app` directory. They are the equivalent of [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes) inside the `pages` directory meaning you **do not** need to use API Routes and Route Handlers together.
### Convention
Route Handlers are defined in a [`route.js|ts` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) inside the `app` directory:
```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
export async function GET(request: Request) {}
```
```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
export async function GET(request) {}
```
Route Handlers can be nested anywhere inside the `app` directory, similar to `page.js` and `layout.js`. But there **cannot** be a `route.js` file at the same route segment level as `page.js`.
### Supported HTTP Methods
The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. If an unsupported method is called, Next.js will return a `405 Method Not Allowed` response.
### Extended `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` APIs
In addition to supporting the native [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs, Next.js extends them with [`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) and [`NextResponse`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response) to provide convenient helpers for advanced use cases.
### Caching
Route Handlers are not cached by default. You can, however, opt into caching for `GET` methods. Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached. To cache a `GET` method, use a [route config option](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) such as `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` in your Route Handler file.

content.text:
Managers can now set the weights by writing an instruction on the Settings page: the AI proposes the settings and nothing changes until they apply them. I tested it end to end in a browser with your OpenAI key. Types and lint pass, and the two changed diagrams render without errors.

**How it works** (sliders icon in the top bar → `/dashboard/settings`):
- **Write the rule:** a "Tell Dixi in your words" box sits above the sliders, with four example instructions you can click.
- **Suggest settings:** the AI returns a short summary, a **Now → Proposed** table for each changed setting, and one sentence per change explaining why.
- **Apply or Discard:** Apply moves the sliders and the live example updates immediately.
- **Change log:** every applied change records the instruction, the person and role, the date and time, and whether the AI or the simple fallback proposed it.

**What the test showed:** "For the 7 Series, past rejects should count for two years and hardly ever come back" produced:
- **Reject penalty:** 60% → 100%
- **Memory:** 365 → 730 days
- **Resurface threshold:** +30% → +150%

After Apply, a request "rejected today" scores 0 in the example instead of 33. My test browser now has these settings, while yours still has the defaults.

**Safety and limits:**
- **Key on the server only:** the key is never sent to the browser; it's read from your git-ignored `.env`.
- **Limited answers:** the model can only answer in a fixed format, and every value is clamped to its allowed range.
- **Speed:** a request takes about 6–7 seconds; the first call after a restart took 30 seconds.
- **Without a key** (the public Vercel site has none): a simple keyword fallback still proposes changes and is labelled as such.
- **Settings are global:** they apply to **every** series and market. The AI now says so when an instruction names a single series. Per-series settings would be the natural next step.

**Architecture docs:**
- **`09-scoring-and-memory.md`:** a new "Tell Dixi in your words" section with the five steps, the flow added to the diagram, and the backend plan (tables for settings and for the change log).
- **`06-web-app.md`:** the Settings page and the new server route.
- **`docs/README.md` and `docs/requirements.md`:** mention plain-words settings and the server-only key.
- **`web/.env.example`:** now lists the server-only `OPENAI_API_KEY` and model name. For the live site, the key would go into Vercel's settings, and I'll only do that if you ask.

Still open: **three markets (Europe, China, USA), or the UK instead of Japan?**
